analysis:
This PR adds only a test file, scripts/models/test_model_requant_upload.py (mode 100644). It touches no provider runtime, coordinator, attestation or cache code, so I found no regression against the retained provider threat model (T-041, TB-007 and others). The model weights, R2 credentials and workflow it exercises (A-004, A-011 and similar) are mostly outside the retained scope, which excludes backend and publishing infrastructure.

The tests run as ordinary unit tests. They use a fake aws/python3 shell script in a temp directory, a loopback HTTP server bound to 127.0.0.1, and subprocess calls to the repo's own scripts. Fixture credentials are dummy strings (prod-key-id, legacy-secret and an invented R2-shaped endpoint), not real secrets. The tests assert security-relevant workflow properties: runs only from master, secrets confined to the prod-environment job after a secret-free preflight, hash-pinned pip installs, no ${{ }} interpolation inside run scripts, endpoint digits not leaked to logs, and the GITHUB_OUTPUT newline-injection refusal. These add protective regression coverage and no new attack surface.

Limits: the unit-3 head text stops at line 522, and units 1 and 2 are patch excerpts, so the whole file was covered only through those patches. The workflow YAML, upload-model-revision.py, requant.py, requirements-requant-upload.txt and testdata were not supplied. I cannot verify that the tests match those artifacts or that the workflow really enforces these controls. The tests also parse the YAML with a regex-based parser, which could miss structures. The integration pass should review those companion files if they are in the PR.
